brief: Separate money for a predictable bill from money for an unforeseen disruption.

en-US.scenario: Fictional US-dollar examples for "Saving Purposes"; illustrative amounts, not current prices or product offers. No assumption of salary, bank ownership or spare income.

es-MX.scenario: Ejemplos ficticios en pesos mexicanos para "Cuentas previstas e imprevistos"; montos ilustrativos, no precios vigentes ni ofertas. No se supone nómina, cuenta bancaria ni dinero sobrante.

pt-BR.scenario: Exemplos fictícios em reais para "Contas previstas e imprevistos"; valores ilustrativos, não preços atuais nem ofertas. Sem supor salário, conta bancária ou dinheiro sobrando.

objective.observable_action: Separate money for a predictable bill from money for an unforeseen disruption.
objective.success_criterion: Complete the fresh-context transfer using only its visible information.

instruction.relevance: A bill can be infrequent without being unexpected; give planned expenses and disruptions separate space in your savings plan.
instruction.misconception: Every nonmonthly bill is an emergency, or a known annual payment needs no advance saving.
instruction.numeracy_support: Use only the visible fictional amounts and conditions; earlier arithmetic is preparation, not a hidden financial assumption.

evidence.reasoning: Save ahead for known dates and amounts. An emergency reserve serves unexpected disruptions, rather than replacing every planned bill fund.
Known annual payments can be planned before their due date.
The unexpected essential failure differs from a scheduled expense.
Size alone does not turn a known payment into a surprise.
Separate purposes prevent counting the same money for both needs.
A repeating known obligation can be saved for in advance.
The known premium and sudden damage have different saving purposes.

delayed_retrieval.fresh_context: Retrieve this competence in the declared later course reviews and through the existing shared review system.
